ui_bugs.issue: summary-promo-error message is set inside applyPromo() then immediately cleared by the useEffect on next render. When user enters invalid code (e.g. FAKE99), applyPromo() sets the error AND calls clearPromo(). clearPromo() updates localStorage so on re-render `const promo = getPromo()` returns null, the useEffect re-runs with new `promo` dep, and its else branch `setPromoError('')` wipes the error. Net result: rejection is fully silent — user sees no feedback. Spec asked the error to say 'isn\'t valid'. Fix: don't reset promoError in the useEffect when promo is null, OR use a useRef/separate state flag to indicate 'last apply was rejected'.

rca of the issue: Invalid-promo error UX bug RCA: In SummaryCard.jsx, applyPromo() → setPromo(code) writes to localStorage → React re-renders → top-level `const promo = getPromo()` returns 'FAKE99' → useEffect fires with new `promo` dep → getQuote returns no promo_code → `if (promo && (!q.promo_code...))` matches → setPromoError(...) GOOD. BUT applyPromo's own .then() also fires (race) and calls clearPromo() because the server returned no promo. clearPromo() → next React render → `promo = getPromo()` now returns null → useEffect fires again with promo=null dep → first if-branch (`if (promo && ...)`) fails because promo is falsy → ELSE branch runs → setPromoError('') wipes the error. The user sees nothing. Reproduction: clean localStorage, navigate to /booking, select Standard Room, click 'Have a promo code?', type 'FAKE99', click Apply. Wait 2 seconds. Observe summary-promo-error not visible. Mitigation: either (a) gate the useEffect's setPromoError('') behind an explicit condition like `if (promo && q.promo_code) setPromoError('')`, or (b) move error state into a useRef that only the apply handler touches, or (c) don't call clearPromo() inside applyPromo's rejection branch — leave the invalid code in LS until the next attempt so the useEffect's error-setting branch keeps firing.
